title: Canonical Reduction Strategy Correctness

basis.scope: Bounded correctness of canonical reduction strategy S(C) for admissible continuation classes satisfying the previously established operational properties; process equivalence, canonical outcomes, bounded determinism, and bounded confluence assumptions are preserved, and no universal correctness or optimality claim is made.

core_rule.statement: Canonical reduction strategy correctness applies only after EVAL_024 and only to bounded continuation classes satisfying WF(C), Typed(C), Det(C), Term(C), Unique(C), and Conf_B(C); S(C) preserves process equivalence, canonical reduction outcomes, bounded determinism, bounded confluence assumptions, and canonical representative selection modulo ≡P; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Establish the bounded correctness of the canonical reduction strategy S(C). This theorem shows that the strategy preserves the established operational properties of the RT Calculus for admissible continuation classes without asserting universal correctness.

canonical_claims.statement: Canonical strategy correctness is only evaluated after EVAL_024 has succeeded.
Only admissible candidates participate in canonical strategy selection.
Canonical strategy correctness preserves process equivalence and canonical reduction outcomes.
Canonical strategy correctness preserves bounded determinism and bounded confluence assumptions.

formal_objects.name: Canonical Strategy Correctness
formal_objects.definition: The property that the canonical reduction strategy preserves lawful reduction semantics for bounded continuation classes.

formal_objects.name: Correctness Class
formal_objects.definition: Continuation classes satisfying all bounded correctness prerequisites.

then: S(C) produces the same canonical representative modulo ≡P.

correctness_obligations.description: S(C) operates only after successful EVAL_024.
Process equivalence is maintained throughout reduction.
Canonical outcomes remain NF(C), pNF(C), or ⊥C_x.

limitations: Applies only to bounded continuation classes.
Does not claim minimal runtime complexity.
